extracted.intended_audience: Small business SBIR/STTR applicants and PIs preparing Phase I biotechnology/preclinical vaccine proposals (PIs, grant writers, institutional grants administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and justifying a Phase I SBIR/STTR proposal (research plan and budget justification) for a preclinical biotech vaccine project, including personnel, subawards, animal studies, budgets, and required PHS/OMB attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification — personnel salaries and staffing levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific personnel salaries and related expenses represent 52% of TechnoVax expenses or 41% of Total Requested Funds. High salaries costs are driven by two main factors: (1) the project duration and (2) the higher cost of salaries in the New York metro area. To attract adequate talent TechnoVax needs to offer competitive salaries; however ... our salaries are still about +30% lower than those offered at other larger biotech companies located within a 10 miles radius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain percent of budget devoted to salaries, justify regional salary levels and competitiveness with local industry, and show staffing is adequate and financially balanced. Provide comparisons to local employers to justify rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel roles, percent effort and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: PI and key personnel should have clearly defined roles, percent effort, and justification. Example: PI (Dr. Jose M. Galarza) will allocate 25% effort and oversee/participate in creation, production, characterization and testing; Staff Scientist (Dr. Diana Dalfo) 60% effort; Research Associate 100% effort; Research Intern full-time for 18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each senior/key person, their project role, percent effort, proportional salary requested per budget period, and brief justification of duties and qualifications. Include CV/biographical support in attachments or letters of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits and salary escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe Benefits: Based on current payroll data, Fringe Benefits amount to 25% of Base Salary Costs. Salary and Costs increases: a 3% annual increase has been budgeted for salaries in period 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State fringe benefit rate and basis (e.g., payroll data). If budgeting future increases, state assumed % and apply consistently across periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment justification (small equipment needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Miscellaneous Equipment: as current lab equipment is mostly fully utilized by current projects, various small equipment items will be needed for day to day operations (fridge, -20C freezer, etc.). [An amount] has been budgeted annually to cover purchases and maintenance costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify why existing equipment is insufficient, list needed items and per-item or annual budget, and explain relation to project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic Travel: $ in year 1 is budgeted for attending a major scientific conference and scientific meetings as follows: PI or Staff Scientist: ( $ for registration and $ for travel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify conferences/meetings, who will attend, and break down registration and travel costs. Tie travel to dissemination/outreach or project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other direct costs — materials and supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Material and supplies: General laboratory supplies including plastic-ware, reagents, chemicals, tissue culture media and protein analysis and purification material, Western blot reagent, disposables are requested for vaccine production, characterization and testing. This total budget of $ over 2 years is based on a current comparable project for the production of an influenza VLP vaccine and can be broken down into categories by year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic, project-based supplies estimate, justify by comparison to similar projects, and break down major categories and by budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment or facility rental/user fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Electron-Microscopy images will be needed after each production batch; we currently use City College of New York (CUNY) EM equipment for a cost of per session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for shared/core facility fees with per-session costs and frequency tied to project milestones (e.g., EM after each batch). Include justification for use of external facilities and estimated number of sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs / F&A rate justification
rubrics_metrics.description: F&A costs: as awarded in previous SBIR grants, we are requesting a 25% indirect cost rate applied to direct costs to cover F&A costs. (Elsewhere, Baylor's negotiated rate is stated as 56.50% with DHHS.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the indirect cost rate being claimed, reference prior awards or negotiated agreements, indicate indirect cost base, and include cognizant federal agency contact information if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee request (profit/fee) justification
rubrics_metrics.description: TechnoVax requests 6.99% fixed fee for re-investment into company infrastructure and Operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including a fee, state percentage, intended use, and ensure it complies with agency rules for SBIR/STTR fee limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward justification and budgeting (BSL facility costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our sub-awardee, Dr. Innocent Mbawuike at Baylor College of Medicine, will perform the animal studies and is budgeting $ or about 20% of total requested funds. This cost is justified by the fact that these studies will need to take place in BSL-2 and 'BSL-3 enhanced' level facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For subcontracted work, include subaward budget forms, list senior/key personnel and effort at subawardee site, justify why subaward is necessary (e.g., specialized BSL facility), and attach subaward budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal costs, housing and vivarium fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal purchase and housing: Approximately 250 young adult mice will be purchased for ($ each). The cost for housing animals in the biohazard suite of BCM vivarium is based on $ for mice (4 mice per cage) per diem respectively. It is estimated that the animals will be housed for approximately 60 days during each experiment for a cost of [amount].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify numbers of animals, per-animal and per-diem housing costs, duration, and relate costs to experimental design. Include vertebrate animal justification and attach required animal welfare approvals/attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR eligibility and certification questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SBIR/STTR information: certify small business eligibility at time of award; disclose subcontracts with federal labs; HUBZone status; whether all R&D will be performed in the U.S.; whether essentially equivalent work has been submitted elsewhere; disclosure permission for non-awarded proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer all required SBIR/STTR checklist questions, attach explanatory files where required, and ensure eligibility criteria (e.g., company size, PI employment rules) are met and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization plan requirement (Phase II / Fast-Track)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization Plan: If you are submitting a Phase II or Phase I/Phase II Fast-Track Application, include a Commercialization Plan in accordance with the agency announcement and/or agency-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a commercialization plan when required by solicitation; describe market, regulatory pathway (e.g., IND plans), and commercialization strategy; include as an attachment per agency instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR PI employment and workshare requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions regarding PI employment: Will the Project Director/PI have primary employment with the small business at the time of award? For STTR: (1) Does the PI have a formal appointment or commitment either with the small business OR as an employee of the Research Institution with a commitment to the small business; AND (2) Will the PI devote at least 10% effort? In joint R&D, small business must perform >=40% and research institution >=30% of the work (STTR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document PI's employment status and percent effort; for STTR, provide workshare calculations and supporting institutional commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Research Plan attachments and PHS 398 sections
rubrics_metrics.description: List of Research Plan Attachments: Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Protection of Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women and Minorities; Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table; Inclusion of Children; Vertebrate Animals; Select Agent Research; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plan(s); Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach applicable sections of the research plan as required by PHS 398. Ensure each required attachment is present and labeled correctly (file names shown in form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — clear, testable objectives tied to impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should state the overall goal (e.g., develop a broadly neutralizing influenza VLP vaccine), the rationale (expose conserved subdominant antigenic sites), and a set of concrete aims: (1) construct remodeled HA and produce/characterize VLPs; (2) assess immune response in mice via micro-neutralization assay and test combinations; (3) conduct efficacy and immunogenicity studies in lethal mouse models and plan for ferret/Phase II/IND enabling data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write succinct, achievable aims that map to experiments and endpoints, and indicate downstream plans (e.g., Phase II, IND) if relevant for SBIR commercialization pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy — Significance and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy must describe the significance and public health impact: burden of disease, limitations of current vaccines, rationale for VLP approach, prior identification of broadly neutralizing antibodies, and how project could address antigenic drift/shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate compelling public health need, provide epidemiological context and literature citations, and explain how the project addresses a gap or offers an innovative solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and feasibility — clarity and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary results must be described clearly and provide convincing feasibility evidence. Prior reviewers noted preliminary results were not described clearly and thus did not convincingly show feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present preliminary experiments and data in sufficient detail (methods, controls, assays, representative data) to support feasibility. Revise unclear sections and explain how preliminary data inform proposed tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk mitigation and alternative plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Address reviewer concerns about over-ambitious scope and lack of alternate plans. Example mitigation: design multiple remodeled HA constructs (including 5TA with protease cleavage sites) and enlist structural biologist collaborator to strengthen design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contingency strategies and multiple technical approaches to reduce programmatic risk; explain decision points and go/no-go criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay selection and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify choice of assays: primary evaluation by virus neutralization (measures neutralizing activity), ELISA proposed as a secondary method to detect binding antibodies using virus as target antigen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what each assay measures, why it was selected, and how results will be interpreted relative to project goals (e.g., neutralization vs binding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing approach and scalability justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe production strategy and scalability: initial transient transfection into cell line constitutively expressing M1/M2 for candidate screening, followed by creation of constitutively producing vaccine cell line for candidates — argued to be faster and more cost-effective than current seasonal vaccine manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic manufacturing plan for candidate production, discuss scalability, cost and timeline implications, and compare to existing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators, letters of support and subaward attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters (e.g., structural biologist Dr. Zhongtoa Zhang, subaward LOI/letters from Dr. Mbawuike) describing collaborator roles and commitments. Subaward budget justification file referenced (e.g., 1243-BAYLOR_BudgetJustification_120512.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach signed letters of support/LOIs that document collaborator expertise, roles, and institutional resources. Include subaward budget justification and personnel listings in subaward attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and HESC questions
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement: indicate whether human subjects are involved, whether this is an Agency-Defined Phase III clinical trial, and whether human embryonic stem cells (HESC) are used (if so list registry numbers or indicate a registry line will be used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer human subjects and HESC questions fully on the cover supplement; include protection of human subjects section if applicable; provide registry numbers or statements about lines to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and data sharing plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plan(s) are listed among required attachments (e.g., data/resource sharing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any required data sharing, material sharing, or public access plans per agency policy as attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with PHS 398 and OMB form structure for budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Research & Related budget forms: Section A Senior/Key Person; Section B Other Personnel; Section C Equipment; Section D Travel; Section E Participant/Trainee Support; Section F Other Direct Costs (Materials and Supplies, Publication Costs, Consultant Services, ADP, Subawards, Equipment/Facility Rental, Alterations and Renovations); Section G Direct Costs; Section H Indirect Costs; Section I Total Direct and Indirect Costs; Section J Fee. Include Budget Justification file and subaward files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all budget sections according to PHS 398 instructions, attach budget justification and subaward documentation, and ensure totals and categories are consistent across forms and justification.
